item.text: I’ll use only the brief and candidate list already in this conversation to add omitted passages. I won’t read or recheck files; I’ll write a separate TSV with new rows only.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > /Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec11/luna/followup.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.11.4	righteous judgment; rod of the mouth strikes earth; breath kills the wicked	Isaiah's just ruler judges the poor rightly, strikes the earth with his mouth's rod, and kills the wicked by his breath; this is a close verbal-impact counterpart to the commentary's haqq as a direct, penetrating blow against batil.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.23.29	God's word as fire and a hammer breaking rock	Jeremiah compares God's word to fire and a hammer that shatters rock; this gives the commentary's haqq-as-projectile a second image of forceful impact and adds the destruction of hard resistance.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.55.11	sent word accomplishes its purpose and does not return empty	Isaiah compares God's sent word to rain that makes the earth fruitful and says it accomplishes its purpose; this is a precise counter-image to the commentary's missed strike, where the true word reaches its intended result.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.5.14	prophetic words made fire that consumes the people	God makes his words in Jeremiah's mouth fire and the people wood to be consumed; this turns speech into a forceful strike, while casting its target as a resistant people under judgment.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.30.14	word near in mouth and heart in order to do it	Deuteronomy places the command in mouth and heart so it can be done; this joins inward reception to action, sharpening the commentary's image of haqq entering the body and amal as force put to work.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.31.33	Torah written within and on the heart	In the new-covenant promise, God writes Torah on the people's inward parts and hearts; this gives the commentary's penetrating strike an inward inscription counterpart and makes its truth a lasting disposition.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.8.8	wise woman's words are righteous and not crooked	Wisdom says all her words are righteous, with none crooked or perverse; this explicitly joins truth and straightness, the commentary's haqq and its contrast between a true line and deviation.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.8.9	wise words are straight to the discerning	Wisdom's words are clear and straight to those who understand; this adds the hearer's recognition of alignment to the commentary's straight-shot image.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 28:17	tongue's blow breaks bones	Sirach contrasts a whip's bruise with a tongue's blow that breaks bones; it gives speech the commentary's bodily force and inward reach, while emphasizing harmful speech rather than haqq.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 28:18	more are fallen by the tongue than by the sword	Sirach says more people fall through the tongue than through the sword; this intensifies the commentary's weapon image by making speech more destructive than physical arms.
medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 5:17-20	justice as armor; wrath sharpened as a sword	In its judgment scene, Wisdom clothes God in righteousness and justice and sharpens wrath as a sword; this gives the commentary's moral conflict a divine-war image while assigning the blade to judgment rather than to haqq itself.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Dan.7.13	source word ٱلْإِنسَٰن root ء ن س / Aramaic אֱנָשׁ; table's sound correspondence only, unverified	The source ayah labels al-insan with root ء ن س; Daniel's Aramaic vision uses anash for a human-like figure coming with the clouds, a distinct singular use of the table's tentative correspondence rather than the commentary's general humanity.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.7.14	human-like figure receives dominion and an everlasting kingdom	Daniel gives the human-like figure dominion and a kingdom serving all peoples; this adds an exalted apocalyptic human counter-image to the commentary's human set as target and the ayah's general loss.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Eccl.4.8	Arabic source roots ع م ل / Hebrew עמל and خ س ر / Hebrew חסר; both table correspondences unverified	Qoheleth describes unending toil and asks why the solitary worker labors while depriving himself of good; the verse brings the table's tentative work and lack correspondences together as effort that leaves a person without its benefit, contrasting the commentary's aimed action.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.4.9	two workers have good return for their toil	Qoheleth says two are better than one because their toil has a good return; this gives the commentary's action and mutual counsel a concrete cooperative setting, in which shared effort improves the result.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.4.10	one companion lifts the other when he falls	The passage says one companion can lift the other after a fall; this makes the commentary's mutual counsel to patience practical support against a person's loss of footing.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.10.10	blunt iron takes more force; wisdom brings success	Qoheleth says blunt iron requires more strength, while wisdom helps one succeed; this is a concrete tool-and-force image beside the commentary's spear, whose directed action must make an effective strike.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Prov.14.23	Arabic source root خ س ر / Hebrew חסר; table's sound correspondence only, unverified	The commentary glosses source khusr as loss; Proverbs uses the Hebrew lack form and contrasts profit in labor with poverty from mere talk, giving the tentative root pairing a concrete outcome of failed effort.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.14.23	profit from labor contrasted with lack from mere talk	Proverbs says toil yields profit but mere speech leads to lack; this speaks to the commentary's distinction between forceful action and loss, adding a warning that words without effective work can leave a deficit.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.7.13	the broad road leads to destruction	Jesus describes a broad way leading to destruction; this makes the commentary's khusr-as-deviation a path with a stated end, and contrasts the many who take it with the ayah's exception.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.7.14	the narrow way leads to life and few find it	Jesus contrasts the difficult way leading to life, found by few, with destruction's broad way; this adds the exception's narrow, directed course to the commentary's loss-as-deviation image.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.5.19	one among the community wanders from the truth and is brought back	James describes a believer wandering from truth and another person bringing him back; this closely joins the commentary's deviation from the line to its mutual counsel in haqq.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.5.20	turning a sinner back saves a soul from death	James says the person who turns a sinner back from his erring way saves him from death; this makes correction of deviation a concrete rescue from loss.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.2.37	listeners are pierced in the heart by Peter's proclamation	After Peter's speech, listeners are pierced in the heart and ask what to do; this gives the commentary's truthful impact an inward human response and connects penetration to changed action.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.19.34	a soldier pierces Jesus' side with a spear	John recounts a soldier piercing Jesus' side and blood and water emerging; this is a literal bodily counterpart to the commentary's lance entering the inside, while its passion context makes the pierced person a victim rather than a target of righteous counsel.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.14.12	saints' endurance with God's commandments and faith	Revelation identifies the saints by endurance, keeping God's commandments, and faith; this directly brings sabr together with belief and action, adding an apocalyptic picture of the ayah's exception.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.4.2	preach the word, correct and exhort with patience	Paul tells Timothy to proclaim the word, correct, rebuke, and exhort with all patience; this closely combines the commentary's truth and reciprocal advice with sabr as the manner of correction.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Col.3.16	Christ's word teaches and admonishes people mutually	The community is to let Christ's word dwell richly as its members teach and admonish one another; this gives the commentary's mutual counsel to truth a word-centered communal form, with song and thanksgiving as its setting.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.3.13	daily mutual exhortation guards against sin's deception	Hebrews commands daily mutual exhortation so no one hardens through sin's deceit; this links the commentary's counsel in truth to preventing a person's deviation and adds a daily communal practice.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.1.3	testing produces endurance	James says the testing of faith produces endurance; this describes sabr as formed under pressure, giving the commentary's human target image a process of remaining steadfast through impact.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.1.4	endurance completes its work so one lacks nothing	James says endurance should complete its work so a person becomes complete and lacks nothing; this joins the commentary's sabr and amal to an explicit overcoming of lack.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.6	love rejoices with the truth	Paul says love does not rejoice in wrongdoing but rejoices with truth; this gives the commentary's haqq a communal ethical setting, where truth marks the difference between right and wrong action.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.7	love bears and endures all things	Paul describes love as bearing and enduring all things; this supplies a relational form of sabr alongside the commentary's reciprocal counsel, distinct from mere aim or force.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.13	make straight paths for the feet so the lame may heal	Hebrews commands straight paths for feet so the lame limb may be healed rather than dislocated; this combines the commentary's straight trajectory with its bodily penetration image, and turns straightness toward restoration.
EOF"
